questions.question: Friction is a force that opposes:
options: Motion between two surfaces in contact
questions.explanation: Friction is the force that opposes relative motion between two surfaces in contact. It acts along the surfaces and opposes sliding or rolling.

questions.question: Friction acts in a direction:
questions.explanation: Friction always acts opposite to the direction of relative motion (or attempted motion) between the surfaces.

questions.question: The force that opposes the start of motion between two surfaces is:
questions.explanation: Static friction is the force that must be overcome to start motion between two surfaces at rest.

questions.question: The force that opposes motion when one surface slides over another is:
questions.explanation: Kinetic friction (sliding friction) opposes motion when one surface slides over another.

questions.question: Rolling friction is generally:
questions.explanation: Rolling friction is generally much less than sliding friction, which is why wheels and ball bearings reduce friction.

questions.question: Which of the following is a way to reduce friction?
questions.explanation: Lubrication (e.g., oil or grease) reduces friction by separating surfaces. Increasing roughness, normal reaction, or load increases friction.

questions.question: Which of the following is a way to increase friction?
questions.explanation: Making surfaces rough increases friction. Polishing, lubricating, and using ball bearings reduce friction.

questions.question: The coefficient of friction is defined as the ratio of:
questions.explanation: The coefficient of friction (μ) is defined as μ = F/N, where F is the frictional force and N is the normal reaction.

questions.question: The coefficient of friction has:
questions.explanation: Since μ is a ratio of two forces, it has no unit (dimensionless).

questions.question: Static friction is:
questions.explanation: For most surfaces, static friction is greater than kinetic friction. This is why it is harder to start motion than to keep it going.

questions.question: The limiting frictional force is:
questions.explanation: The limiting frictional force is the maximum value of static friction just before motion begins.

questions.question: The frictional force between two surfaces depends on:
questions.explanation: Friction depends on the normal reaction and the nature of the surfaces, not on the area of contact.

questions.question: For a given pair of surfaces, kinetic friction is:
questions.explanation: Kinetic friction is approximately independent of speed for moderate speeds.

questions.question: The normal reaction on a body of mass m resting on a horizontal surface is:
questions.explanation: On a horizontal surface, the normal reaction balances the weight: N = mg.

questions.question: If the normal reaction is 50 N and frictional force is 10 N, the coefficient of friction is:
A block of mass 10 kg rests on a horizontal surface. If coefficient of static friction is 0.4, the limiting friction is [g = 10 m/s²]:
questions.explanation: N = mg = 10 × 10 = 100 N. Limiting friction = μN = 0.4 × 100 = 40 N.

questions.question: The angle of friction is the angle whose tangent is:
questions.explanation: The angle of friction θ satisfies tan θ = μ, where μ is the coefficient of friction.

questions.question: If coefficient of friction is 1, the angle of friction is:
questions.explanation: tan θ = μ = 1, so θ = 45°.

questions.question: A body just begins to slide on an inclined plane at 30°. The coefficient of static friction is:
questions.explanation: At the angle of repose, μ = tan θ. θ = 30°, so μ = tan 30° = 1/√3 ≈ 0.58.

questions.question: A body just begins to slide on an inclined plane at 45°. The coefficient of friction is:
Friction can be reduced by using:
questions.explanation: Ball bearings convert sliding friction into rolling friction, which is much smaller, thus reducing friction.

questions.question: The type of friction experienced by a wheel rolling on a surface is:
questions.explanation: A wheel rolling on a surface experiences rolling friction, which is less than sliding friction.

questions.question: Viscous friction occurs:
questions.explanation: Viscous friction occurs in fluids (liquids and gases) due to internal friction between layers moving relative to each other.

questions.question: Which of the following is an advantage of friction?
questions.explanation: Friction enables walking by providing grip between shoes and the ground. Wear, reduced efficiency, and unwanted heat are disadvantages.

questions.question: Which of the following is a disadvantage of friction?
options: It causes wear of machine parts
It enables writing with a pen
questions.explanation: A major disadvantage of friction is that it causes wear of machine parts and wastes energy as heat.

questions.question: The force required to just move a body along a horizontal surface is equal to:
questions.explanation: The minimum force to start motion equals the limiting static friction.

questions.question: If a body is moving with constant velocity on a rough horizontal surface, the applied force is:
questions.explanation: For constant velocity, net force = 0, so applied force = kinetic friction.

questions.question: The frictional force on a body moving on a rough horizontal surface is 12 N. If the normal reaction is 60 N, the coefficient of kinetic friction is:
When the normal reaction is doubled, the frictional force:
questions.explanation: Since F = μN, if N doubles, F doubles.

questions.question: Which surface will produce the greatest friction with a moving block?
questions.explanation: Rough concrete has the highest coefficient of friction among the options.

questions.question: The efficiency of a machine is reduced by:
questions.explanation: Friction converts useful mechanical energy into heat, thus reducing efficiency.

questions.question: The purpose of lubrication in machines is to:
questions.explanation: Lubrication reduces friction by separating moving surfaces with a fluid layer.

questions.question: Friction between two surfaces can be reduced by:
questions.explanation: Applying oil (lubrication) reduces friction. The other options increase friction.

questions.question: The frictional force that opposes the motion of a body through air is called:
questions.explanation: Air resistance (drag) is the frictional force opposing motion through air.

questions.question: A car tyre has treads to:
questions.explanation: Treads increase friction between the tyre and the road, improving grip and safety.

questions.question: Brakes in a vehicle work by:
questions.explanation: Brakes work by increasing friction between brake pads and the wheel/disc, converting kinetic energy to heat.

questions.question: A block of mass 5 kg is pulled along a horizontal surface with a force of 15 N. If coefficient of kinetic friction is 0.2, the acceleration is [g = 10 m/s²]:
questions.explanation: N = mg = 50 N. Friction f = μN = 0.2×50 = 10 N. Net force = 15 − 10 = 5 N. a = F_net/m = 5/5 = 1.0 m/s².

questions.question: In question 37, frictional force is:
questions.explanation: Frictional force = μN = 0.2 × 50 = 10 N.

questions.question: The maximum value of static friction is called:
questions.explanation: The maximum static friction is called limiting friction.

questions.question: A body of weight 100 N rests on a horizontal surface. If coefficient of static friction is 0.3, the minimum force to start motion is:
questions.explanation: N = 100 N. Minimum force = μN = 0.3 × 100 = 30 N.

questions.question: The friction between two surfaces in contact is independent of:
questions.explanation: Friction is independent of the area of contact (for a given normal reaction and surface pair).

questions.question: When a body slides on a rough surface, the frictional force is:
questions.explanation: Friction always acts opposite to the direction of motion.

questions.question: A body moving on a rough surface comes to rest eventually because:
options: Friction converts kinetic energy to heat
questions.explanation: Friction does negative work, converting kinetic energy into heat, so the body slows down and stops.

questions.question: The coefficient of friction between two surfaces is 0.25. If the normal reaction is 80 N, the frictional force is:
Which of the following pairs has the highest coefficient of friction?
questions.explanation: Rubber on concrete has a very high coefficient of friction (often > 1), making it ideal for tyres.

questions.question: The force that opposes the relative motion between layers of a fluid is:
questions.explanation: Viscosity is the internal friction that opposes relative motion between layers of a fluid.

questions.question: The coefficient of static friction is generally:
questions.explanation: For most surfaces, static friction is greater than kinetic friction, so μ_s > μ_k.

questions.question: A block just slides when the applied force is 20 N. If the normal reaction is 100 N, the coefficient of static friction is:
A body is placed on an inclined plane. As the angle of inclination increases, the component of weight parallel to the plane:
questions.explanation: The component of weight parallel to the plane is mg sin θ. As θ increases, sin θ increases, so the component increases.

questions.question: The main reason for using ball bearings in machines is to:
options: Convert sliding friction to rolling friction
questions.explanation: Ball bearings convert sliding friction into rolling friction, which is much smaller, reducing energy losses.
